_readme: All resume text lives here. Edit this file and push to GitHub; the live site updates automatically. The page shows each job's 'key' bullets (3 is best) and hides 'creative', 'highlights', and 'earlier_roles' behind a 'More' link. Work items with "featured": true show first; the rest appear under 'See all work'. The 'intro' block sets the welcome pop-up's text, choices, and delay; answers are saved to the visitor_intros table in Supabase. A job's optional 'since' note (for example 'At Fromm since 2005') shows under its dates. A certificate's 'status' (for example "Completed" or "In progress, Fall 2026") shows next to it; anything not completed is left out of the data Google reads. The page shows the short versions: each job's 'line' and 'points' (2-3 bullets, 12 words or fewer), each work item's 'caption' and 'tag', 'skills_short', and 'partners'. The longer 'summary', 'key', 'areas', 'tags', and full 'skills' sit behind 'More' and are used for the printed resume.
_work_help: Each item in 'work' is one card. Optional: 'image' (or 'images': a list of {"src", "alt"} for a small gallery) (a picture you put in public/work/, e.g. "/work/poster.jpg"), 'imageFit': "contain" or "contain-light" (show a logo or screenshot whole on a dark or white background instead of cropping it), 'video' (a YouTube or Vimeo link; YouTube also gives the card its picture), 'link' (any web page), 'role', 'collaborators', 'details'. 'category' is one name, or a list of names, from: Web design, Product design, Project design, Print design, Video, Storytelling, Marketing, Events, Collaborations, Technology, AI. Featured pieces can also be case studies: add 'challenge', 'approach', and 'outcome' (with 'role' as your part); the open view then shows them as sections.
